test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of meristematic cells?

options.text: Dense cytoplasm and lack of vacuoles

solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Dense cytoplasm and lack of vacuoles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meristematic cells** are a group of young cells that are in a continuous state of **cell division**. These tissues are found in the growing regions of plants, such as the tips of roots and shoots.
 
• A defining characteristic of these cells is the presence of **dense cytoplasm** and a **large, prominent nucleus**. This is because the cells are metabolically very active and require a high concentration of organelles and genetic material to support rapid division.
 
• **Meristematic cells** generally **lack vacuoles**. In mature plant cells, vacuoles serve as storage for food, waste, and provide turgidity. However, meristematic cells do not need to store these materials as they divide quickly, and a large vacuole might obstruct the process of **mitosis**. ***Hence, the third option is the correct characteristic.***
 
• The **cell walls** of meristematic tissues are **thin** and made primarily of **cellulose**. This thinness allows the cells to expand and divide without the restriction of rigid, thick walls.
 
• These cells are **compactly arranged** without any **intercellular spaces** between them, ensuring a solid mass of dividing tissue at growth points.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Meristematic Tissues:**
 
 
• **Apical Meristem**: Located at the **growing tips of stems and roots**. It is responsible for the **primary growth** of the plant, increasing its overall length.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem**: Found at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (common in monocots like grasses). It helps in the elongation of the internodes and regrowth of parts removed by grazing animals.
 
• **Lateral Meristem**: Occurs on the sides of the plant body (e.g., **vascular cambium** and **cork cambium**). It is responsible for **secondary growth**, which increases the **girth** or thickness of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Differentiation into Permanent Tissues:**
 
 
• Once meristematic cells stop dividing, they undergo **differentiation** to become **permanent tissues**. These can be **Simple Permanent Tissues** (Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma) or **Complex Permanent Tissues** (Xylem and Phloem).
 
• **Parenchyma** cells often have **large central vacuoles** for storage, which distinguishes them from meristematic cells.
 
• **Sclerenchyma** consists of **dead cells** with **thick walls** reinforced with **lignin**, providing mechanical strength.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Dead cells with empty spaces**: This describes **Sclerenchyma** or mature **Xylem vessels**. Meristematic cells must be living to perform cell division. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Thin walls with lignin deposits**: Lignin is a complex polymer that provides rigidity and is typically found in **permanent tissues** like Sclerenchyma or Xylem, not in actively dividing meristems which require flexible cellulose walls. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Thick walls and large vacuoles**: This is a feature of mature, **differentiated cells** like Parenchyma. Thick walls would hinder the rapid expansion and division necessary for meristematic activity. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Metabolic State**: The **respiration rate** in meristematic cells is very high compared to permanent cells because of the energy required for **DNA replication** and cytoplasmic synthesis during the **cell cycle**.
 
• **Shape**: These cells are usually **isodiametric**, meaning they have roughly equal dimensions in all directions, often appearing spherical, oval, or polygonal.
</ul
